key_insight: An explainable deep reinforcement learning framework can optimize residential building energy management while making battery-control decisions more transparent and trustworthy.
engineering_relevance: The approach helps lower electricity costs and improve operational stability in PV-equipped buildings with storage by adapting to dynamic prices, weather, and demand.
method: Train on-policy and off-policy DRL agents for building energy control
Use an expanded state space with demand, PV, battery, SOC, price, weather, calendar, holidays, and forecasts
Apply post-hoc explainability methods to interpret learned policies
evidence_signal: The study compares synthetic data and real-world LLEC/KIT data and reports that A2C and PPO outperform off-policy methods in cumulative reward and policy stability.
watch_item: Because the model depends on high-quality forecasts and real-time signals, performance may degrade if sensor data or price/weather inputs are noisy or missing.
paper_title: Explainable Data-driven Deep Reinforcement Learning Methods for Optimal Energy Management in Buildings
